fixes.explanation: Not this one, friend. The text says Seraiah traveled with King Zedekiah of Judah in the fourth year of Zedekiah's reign (Jeremiah 51:59). Hezekiah isn't the king this verse names. Zedekiah is the one to hold onto.

Not this time, friend. Jeremiah 51:59 says Seraiah went to Babylon with King Zedekiah of Judah, in the fourth year of Zedekiah's reign. Josiah isn't the king this verse names. Zedekiah is the one to hold onto.
Ooh, that would be a much nicer scroll, friend. But the text says Jeremiah wrote about all the disaster that would come upon Babylon (Jeremiah 51:60). Peace isn't what's written on this one.

Not quite, baker. It's False. Jeremiah tells Seraiah, "When you get to Babylon, see that you read all these words aloud…" (Jeremiah 51:61). So he's told to read all the words aloud, not to keep them to himself.

That's right, baker. Jeremiah says, "When you get to Babylon, see that you read all these words aloud…" (Jeremiah 51:61). Seraiah is told to read ALL of it aloud, not keep the words to himself. I'd be asking for a glass of water.

Yes, a stone, baker. Jeremiah says, "When you finish reading this scroll, tie a stone to it and cast it into the Euphrates." (Jeremiah 51:63). A scroll with a stone tied to it is not going to float. Even I could figure out where that ends up.

That's right, baker. Seraiah's last line is "And her people will grow weary." (Jeremiah 51:64). It comes right after the line about Babylon sinking and never rising again. Then the writer closes with "Here end the words of Jeremiah."
